newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African metal workers want 18 to 21 pct pay rise.
newsitem.headline: S.African metal workers want 18 to 21 pct pay rise.

text.p: Annual wage negotiations in the metal and engineering industry kick off next week with unions asking for wage increases between 18 and 21.4 percent, while employers have yet to agree on their offer.
Employer body Steel and Engineering Industries Federation of South Africa (Seifsa) executive director Brian Angus told Reuters employers had not yet put forward a wage offer.
"We will put our offer forward at the first round of talks next week," Angus said.
The first formal round of industry talks is scheduled for April 23 and 24. So far three formal rounds of talks have been planned, Seifsa said in a statement on Wednesday.

Union demands other than wages include a reduction in work hours to 40 per week without loss of pay; an increase in annual leave; an increase in shift work allowances and overtime rates, and the introduction of 200 hours training per worker annually.
Employers' main proposals related to the deregulation of the industry's main agreement as well as job creation initiatives in the industry, Seifsa said.
Around 9,000 companies employing about 285,000 hourly paid workers operate in South Africa's metal and engineering industry.

Workers are represented by nine trade unions, including the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa and the Chemical Workers Industrial Union which are affiliated to the Congress of South African Trade Unions, the country's largest union federation.
